explanation: Keep the lowest earlier price and the best profit seen. Evaluate a sale before allowing its own price to become the next minimum.
correctness: Before each sale, the minimum contains precisely earlier prices. The best sale at that position uses that minimum; maximizing these candidates examines every legal pair implicitly.
walkthrough: For prices [11,7,13,4,10], the first feasible profit is 7-11=-4. Price 7 becomes the cheapest earlier purchase; selling at 13 improves the profit to 6. The later low price 4 followed by 10 also gives 6. Updating the minimum only after considering a sale prevents buying and selling at the same position.
